lessons.title: What Animals Live on a Farm?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name at least four farm animals.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a farm scene picture.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss and name farm animals, matching each to the sound it makes.
resources_needed: Farm animal picture and sound cards
lessons.assessment_notes: Note farm animal vocabulary — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap farm animal names and sounds.
lessons.home_link: Talk about farm animals you know with family.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Old MacDonald Had a Farm' Picture Book
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to join in with repeated phrases from the story/song.
lessons.starter_activity: Sing the familiar song together first.
lessons.main_activity: Read a picture book version, encouraging children to join in with repeated animal sound phrases.
key_questions: What sound does this animal make?
Can you join in with the chorus?

differentiation.extension: Predict the next animal in the story

lessons.assessment_notes: Note participation and prediction — evidence for LIT.1/CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Sing the song together once more.
lessons.home_link: Sing the song with family, adding new animals.

lessons.title: Counting Farm Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count farm animal counters accurately up to 10.
lessons.starter_activity: Count a group of farm animal pictures together.
lessons.main_activity: Children count and sort farm animal counters into a barn/field template, recording totals.
key_questions: Can you count them again to check?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class total farm animal count.
lessons.home_link: Count toy animals or objects at home together.

lessons.title: Making a Farm Animal Mask
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct and decorate a simple animal mask.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at examples of animal masks.
lessons.main_activity: Children choose a farm animal and make/decorate a simple paper mask.
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor and creative choice — evidence for EAD.1/PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Wear masks and make the matching animal sound.
lessons.home_link: Make a simple mask together at home.

lessons.title: What Do Farm Animals Give Us?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name a product that comes from a farm animal.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss where milk comes from.
lessons.main_activity: Match farm animals to the products they give us (cow-milk, sheep-wool, chicken-eggs) using picture cards.
key_questions: What does a cow give us?
What does a sheep give us?

differentiation.extension: Match 4+ pairs and explain uses of the product

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of farm produce — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap farm animal products.
lessons.home_link: Look for farm products (milk, wool, eggs) at home.

lessons.title: Writing Farm Animal Labels
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a simple label for a farm animal.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap farm animal names.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw a farm animal and attempt to write its name using known phonics sounds.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share labelled animal pictures with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Draw and label a farm animal together at home.

lessons.title: Sorting Farm Animals by Number of Legs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sort animals by the number of legs they have.
lessons.starter_activity: Count legs on a chicken vs a cow picture.
lessons.main_activity: Children sort farm animal picture cards into 'two legs' and 'four legs' groups, counting each group.
key_questions: How many legs does this animal have?
How many animals have four legs?

differentiation.extension: Sort 6+ and count totals for each group

lessons.assessment_notes: Note sorting and counting skill — evidence for MATHS.2/MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class tally of both groups.
lessons.home_link: Count legs on animals in pictures or toys at home.

lessons.title: Moving Like Farm Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move imaginatively like different farm animals.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how a horse trots vs a duck waddles.
lessons.main_activity: Children move around the space imitating horses trotting, ducks waddling, and sheep grazing.
key_questions: Can you waddle like a duck?

differentiation.extension: Invent an original farm animal movement

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative movement — evidence for EAD.2/PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss favourite animal movement performed.
lessons.home_link: Act out a farm animal for family.

lessons.title: Baby Farm Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name a baby animal and match it to its parent.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss that a baby sheep is called a lamb.
lessons.main_activity: Match baby animal names/pictures to their parent animal (lamb-sheep, calf-cow, piglet-pig, chick-hen).
resources_needed: Parent and baby animal matching cards
key_questions: What is a baby cow called?
Can you match the baby to its parent?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note vocabulary for animal families — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap baby animal names.
lessons.home_link: Look up baby animal names together at home.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Farmer Duck' by Martin Waddell
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how the animals helped each other in the story.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict from the cover.
lessons.main_activity: Read 'Farmer Duck', discussing how the animals worked together to help the tired duck.
key_questions: How did the other animals help?

differentiation.extension: Explain the animals' teamwork in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and understanding of kindness/teamwork — evidence for LIT.1/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Discuss the story's message about helping each other.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a time you helped someone who was tired or busy.

lessons.title: Doubling Farm Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to double small numbers of farm animals using concrete objects.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap doubling from Week 5.
lessons.main_activity: Children double small quantities of farm animal counters (1-5) and record with drawings.
key_questions: How did you work it out?

differentiation.extension: Double numbers up to 5 and explain method

lessons.assessment_notes: Note doubling understanding progress — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of doubles found.
lessons.home_link: Practise doubling small amounts of toys at home.

lessons.title: Building a Farm Scene
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a small-world farm scene using craft materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a farm layout picture.
lessons.main_activity: Children build a small farm scene using boxes (barn), green paper (field), and craft materials, adding toy animals.
resources_needed: Boxes, green paper, craft materials, toy animals
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe construction and imaginative small-world play — evidence for EAD.1/UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Display farm scenes together.
lessons.home_link: Build a small farm scene together using any materials at home.

lessons.title: A Day in the Life of a Farmer
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what a farmer does.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss who looks after farm animals.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss a farmer's daily tasks (feeding animals, milking cows, collecting eggs) using pictures/role-play props.
key_questions: What does a farmer do each day?

differentiation.extension: Explain the sequence of a farmer's day

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of farming roles — evidence for UTW.3/UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap a farmer's daily tasks.
lessons.home_link: Talk about where your food comes from with family.

lessons.title: Retelling 'Farmer Duck'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the story's key events in sequence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the story from Wednesday.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards, children retell the story sequence using sequencing words and toy animals as props.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group retells to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Farm Animal Patterns
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to continue and create a repeating pattern using farm animal counters.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a simple ABAB animal pattern.
lessons.main_activity: Children continue and create their own repeating pattern using farm animal counters/stickers.
key_questions: What comes next in this pattern?
Can you make your own pattern?

differentiation.support: Continue simple ABAB pattern with support
differentiation.extension: Create own more complex pattern (ABC, ABBA)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note pattern recognition and creation — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Display and admire patterned farm animal sequences.
lessons.home_link: Look for and create patterns with toys at home.

lessons.title: Farm Animal Song and Dance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sing a farm-themed song with actions and animal sounds.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap farm animal movements from Tuesday.
lessons.main_activity: Sing 'Old MacDonald' with actions and matching animal sounds, taking turns to choose the next animal.
key_questions: What animal shall we sing about next?

differentiation.extension: Suggest and lead a new animal verse

lessons.assessment_notes: Note participation and creative contribution — evidence for EAD.2/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Perform the song with all suggested animals.
lessons.home_link: Sing the farm song for family.

lessons.title: Farm Animals Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about farm animals learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's UTW learning.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Farm Animals' display summarising animal names, products, babies, and farmer roles.
key_questions: What have we learned about farm animals?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about farm animals with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Farm Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read simple farm-themed words.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sounds learned this term.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading farm-themed word cards and simple sentences (e.g. 'the pig is in the pen').

differentiation.support: Read simple CVC words with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application to themed vocabulary — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading farm words over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Sorting, Doubling
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, sorting by legs, and doubling skills learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting farm animals, sorting by number of legs, doubling recap.
key_questions: Which group does this belong to?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 25 maths observations.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting and doubling over the weekend.

lessons.title: Farm Animals Celebration Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to combine movement, song, and craft in a class performance.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance combining farm animal movements and the song, with masks and farm scenes displayed.
resources_needed: Craft from the week, music player
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this week?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the farm animals week.
lessons.home_link: Perform a farm animal movement for family this weekend.
